newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica business says fx moves good for confidence.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica business says fx moves good for confidence.

text.p: The latest relaxation of South Africa's foreign exchange controls bodes well for business confidence in the country and signals the country's integration with the world economy, the South African Chamber of Business said on Wednesday.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced earlier that South African individuals, who from July 1 will be allowed to invest offshore for the first time, would be allowed to take a maximum of 200,000 out of the country.

"The measures are in line with the government's macro-economic strategy and represent another important step in the normalisation of South Africa's external financial arrangements," the business chamber said in a statement.
"The announcement also sends a key signal to the outside world of South Africa's continued integration into the world economy."

It said that in view of the fact that local financial markets had had several months to adjust to -- and plan for -- the expected new exchange control situation, it did not beleive there should be any negative impact on the exchange rate.
"The announcement could strengthen business confidence," it said.
It added that with the July 1 relaxations now out of the way, it would now be possible to contemplate a reduction in interest rates in the second half of the year.
